title: Vientiane International Half Marathon 2027 Review: What the 2025 Race Was Like
seo_title: Vientiane Half Marathon Review: Course, Weather, Finish Times
meta_description: Vientiane International Half Marathon review from the 9 March 2025 race: That Luang start, 20°C before dawn, 758 half finishers, a 2:24 median and a fast front.
dek: What the Vientiane International Half Marathon on 9 March 2025 was like: the start at That Luang, the pre-dawn weather, how the field has grown, and how fast you need to be to place.
verdict: Enter if you want a friendly, fast-growing race in Laos's capital with a properly quick front. The 9 March 2025 race had 758 half-marathon finishers, almost twice as many as in 2023, and 1,951 in the 10 km. Weather before dawn was kind: 20°C with a dew point of 16°C and no wind at Wattay airport at 6am, warming to 25°C by 9am. Half the half-marathon field finished inside 2:24, but the top ten were all under 1:21, so this is not a race to win easily. Information is thin: cut-offs and a route map were not published, so plan around a 4.30am start and a warming finish.

sections.heading: The Course: That Luang and the Mekong
paragraphs: In 2025 the race started and finished at That Luang Park, the open ground beside Laos's best-known stupa, with a half marathon, 10 km and 5 km [1]. The route itself was not published in any form found. When the race was run in 2023, it started at 4.30am from the That Luang esplanade and took the half marathon through the city centre and along the Mekong River [2].
The organiser lists the 2027 race for 4.30am [3], so expect the first hour in the dark on city roads. The course is on road [1].

sections.heading: The Weather: Dry and Cool Before Dawn
paragraphs: Wattay International Airport, about 7 km west of That Luang, sent no reports between 1am and 6am on race morning. At 1am and again at 6am it recorded 20°C, a dew point of 16°C, 78% humidity and no wind [4]. It warmed to 21°C at 7.30am and 25°C at 9am, when the dew point had risen to 21°C [4].

On this morning the front of the field ran in near-ideal air. The cost of a slow run is the last hour: with a 4.30am start, as in 2023 and for 2027, a half marathoner on the 2025 median of 2:23:54 finished at about 6.55am, and the slowest 10% were still out after 7.40am, as the sun came up and the temperature climbed [4][5].

sections.heading: Aid Stations and Cut-offs
paragraphs: Entry in 2025 included drink and nutrition stations, medical cover, toilets, a bag drop, a timing chip and a finisher medal [1]; their spacing was not published. No cut-off time was found. The slowest half marathoner in 2025 finished in 3:42:30 and only 2% took longer than three and a half hours [5], so a walker-friendly pace appears to be tolerated.

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: The field nearly doubled between the two editions held here. The half marathon grew from 402 finishers in 2023 to 758 in 2025, and the 10 km from 1,298 to 1,951 [5][6]. With more newcomers the middle of the field slowed: the median half marathon rose from 2:15:33 to 2:23:54, and the median 10 km from 1:20:08 to 1:27:44 [5][6].

The front is quick. The top ten in the 2025 half marathon ran between 1:14:04 and 1:20:25, and the fastest woman was tenth overall in 1:20:25; the tenth woman ran 1:43:41 [5]. In the 10 km the top ten were all inside 37:37 [5]. Behind them, 26.9% of half marathoners broke two hours and 57.4% broke 2:30, and 90% finished inside 3:11:55 [5].
Women made up 18% of half-marathon finishers and 46% of the 10 km [5]. A woman under 1:45 would have been in the top ten of the half in 2025; a man needed to be close to 1:21.

sections.heading: Race Weekend Logistics
paragraphs: In 2025 race packs were collected at the That Luang grounds on Friday 7 and Saturday 8 March, 10am to 6pm, and every runner had to collect their own [1]. Changes of distance were allowed until 28 February, and entries could not be refunded [1].

The race is run by Events for Good, which has organised runs in Laos since 2015, with the Lao Athletics Federation, and supports a local charity [2]. In 2023 every runner got a shirt and half-marathon and 10 km finishers a medal [2].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2027 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a cool-morning half marathon or 10 km in a relaxed capital, and a small, growing field in which a decent club runner can see the leaders. The 10 km is the bigger race and suits first-timers: almost half of its 2025 finishers took longer than 90 minutes [5].
Think twice if you want detailed race information in advance: route, aid spacing and cut-offs were not published for 2025. Run early and steady, because the air warms quickly once the sun is up.
The 2027 race is on Sunday 7 March at 4.30am [3].
This review draws on the race's listings and organiser page, local reporting on the 2023 race, airport weather records and the official results of the 2023 and 2025 races.

faqs.question: What time does the Vientiane International Half Marathon start?
faqs.answer: Before dawn. The organiser lists the 7 March 2027 race for 4.30am, and the 2023 race also started at 4.30am from the That Luang esplanade. In 2025 the race started and finished at That Luang Park. Plan to be at the start well before then, as packs must be collected in advance.

faqs.question: What is the weather like at the Vientiane International Half Marathon?
faqs.answer: Cool and dry before sunrise. On 9 March 2025 Wattay airport recorded 20°C, a dew point of 16°C and no wind at 6am, rising to 21°C at 7.30am and 25°C at 9am. Faster runners finish in good air; slower runners feel the warming in the last hour.

faqs.question: How fast is the Vientiane International Half Marathon?
faqs.answer: Quick at the front, relaxed behind. In 2025 the top ten half marathoners ran 1:14:04 to 1:20:25 and the fastest woman was tenth overall. The median finish was 2:23:54, 26.9% broke two hours and 90% finished inside 3:11:55. The median 10 km took 1:27:44.

faqs.question: Are there shorter races at the Vientiane International Half Marathon?
faqs.answer: Yes. In 2025 the event offered a 10 km and a 5 km alongside the half marathon, and the 10 km was the biggest race, with 1,951 finishers against 758 in the half. Almost half of the 10 km finishers took longer than 90 minutes, so it suits first-timers and walkers.

editorial_notes: Reinstated 2026-11-06: official results for the 9 March 2025 race (and 26 March 2023) are now on file, so the review is written about the 2025 race and attached to the 7 March 2027 edition. A 2026 race was reported held in March 2026 but no results for it are held and nothing about it is used. Finish-time figures are Run SEA's own analysis of the SportStats results; no times were dropped as timing errors. Weather is from Wattay airport METAR observations; the airport sent no reports between 1am and 6am. No 2025 route map, cut-off, aid-station plan or runner account was found; the route description is from the 2023 race. Runners are not named. No rating.
